Wizards 117A look at the Cavs It’s not unreasonable to look at this season as a tale of two halves. While battling injuries and a constant lineup shakeup, the Cavs (52-30) slogged through over half of the regular season raising alarms with their pedestrian play on some nights. That all changed with the acquisition of 11-time NBA All-Star James Harden for injury-plagued All-Star guard Darius Garland prior to the trade deadline. The Core 4 era was officially over, and the expectations surged with an understandable acclimation process. Head coach Kenny Atkinson has trotted out 41 different starting lineups this season. Defensive lapses have been one of the biggest concerns of this particular group, falling as low as 19th in the NBA after the All-Star break. Harden is notorious for his poor defensive play in the postseason during his career. After 26 games together (19-7), this new, refined version of the Cavs are ready for the proving grounds that have consumed the franchise in years past. The stage where every possession is examined under a microscope and individual matchups are methodically dissected.And then there is that familiar word of physicality, which has been a sore subject this time of the year. With Keon Ellis, Dennis Schroeder and Harden in the fray, can Cleveland prove this postseason is different? A look at the RaptorsIn a last-minute push up the standings, Toronto draws the team that eliminated them in three consecutive playoff appearances (2016-18) during LeBron James’ second stint in Cleveland.But in more recent history, the Raptors (46-36) swept the Cavs in three games this season. Here’s the caveat: all of those games took place before Nov. 25, well before Cleveland reinforced its roster. Brandon Ingram (21.5 PPG), RJ Barrett (19.3) and Scottie Barnes (18.1) are the core engine of a revitalized Raptors team that thrives on its fifth-ranked defense and runs a chaotic offense that loves to run. Both will be tested against Cleveland’s star power. Shooting guard Immanuel Quickley could be the X-factor for Toronto’s offense. He is averaging 16.4 points, 5.9 assists and 4.0 rebounds while shooting 44.3% from the field. Quickley recently returned from an eight-game absence due to plantar fasciitis but left the regular season finale with hamstring tightness. The Raptors went a startling 5-22 against the top four seeds in the East and top six seeds in West. What to knowThe Cavs have been bounced from the Eastern Conference Semifinals in the form of a gentleman’s sweep two years in a row. (BOS, IND). They lost in the first round to the New York Knicks three years ago. Cleveland posted the fourth-most points per game during the regular season at 119.5. In 26 games in a Cavaliers uniform, Harden is averaging 20.5 points, 7.7 assists and 4.8 rebounds.All-Star guard Donovan Mitchell is averaging 27.9 points per game, which is seventh in the NBA. He also adds 5.7 assists and 4.5 rebounds. Mitchell has never reached the conference finals in his career.Defending Defensive Player of the Year Evan Mobley has an 11-14 career playoff record. Mobley averages 15.1 points, 9.0 rebounds and 2.0 assists in the postseason. Veteran swingman Max Strus is back from a Jones fracture in his left foot just in time for the playoffs. In 64 playoff games in his career, he averages 9.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 2.2 assists per game while shooting 33.9% from beyond the arc. How can I watch Cavs playoff games on ESPN and ABC for free?If the Cavs are scheduled on ESPN or ABC, you can watch at no cost by utilizing a free trial from DIRECTV and FuboTV. NOTE: ABC games broadcast on DIRECTV will be blacked out due to an ongoing carriage dispute. How do I watch Cavs playoff games on Amazon Prime for free? You can watch Cavs vs. Raptors Eastern Conference Quarterfinals Game 1 on Prime Video at no cost by utilizing a 30-day free trial. Joining Amazon Prime costs $14.99/month or $139 annually. The streaming service features hit shows, blockbusters and live sports. Future playoff streaming optionsIf the Cavs are assigned a game on ESPN, ABC or NBC, here are some other future streaming options. NOTE: ABC AND NBC are not available on DIRECTV (blacked out) and SlingTV (select markets). NBC is not available on Fubo (blacked out). FuboFubo, which offers a free trial and $25 off your first month, has three main packages: Pro costs $73.99/month; Elite is $83.99; Premier is priced at $93.99. Cancel before the free trial ends to avoid being charged. Fubo includes access to more than 185 sports, entertainment and news channels. You can record games, TV shows, movies and more.About DIRECTV DIRECTV, which also gives customers a free trial and $35 off your first month, offers four packages if you continue with the service after your trial ends: Entertainment for $69.99; Choice for $84.99; Ultimate for $109.99; and premier for $159.99. Choice offers the most channels for sports enthusiasts.About Sling TV Sling TV users can get a Day Pass for $4.99; Weekend Pass for $9.99; Week Pass for $14.99; Monthly Pass for $45.99; and Season Pass for $199.99 for 5 months, then $45.99 per month thereafter. You can also subscribe to either the Blue package or the Orange package depending on your viewing preferences. Sling Blue allows up to three streams at a time and Sling Orange allows one stream at a time. About ESPN Streaming The ESPN app now offers an Unlimited Plan for $29.99 per month (or $299.99 for entire year) and a Select Plan for $11.99 per month (or $119.99 for entire year), which replicates its previous coverage of select games and broadcasts on ESPN Plus.
